newsitem.title: Belgium: EU to tell UK BA/American deal must change.
newsitem.headline: EU to tell UK BA/American deal must change.

text.p: The European Commission will tell the British government later on Tuesday it has concluded that a proposed alliance between British Airways and American Airlines would harm fair competition unless changed, a Commission source said.
European Competition Commissioner Karel Van Miert met British Trade and Industry Secretary Margaret Beckett in London to discuss the alliance, a spokesman for Beckett's office said.
He offered no further comment on the talks or the remark by the EU commission source in Brussels that the alliance would meet resistance in its present form.

The Commission's findings had been expected since January this year when Van Miert warned the British government in a letter that the alliance would eliminate competition on many key routes between the United States and Britain.

But the fact that the Commission's position has not changed increases the pressure on Britain, which argues it has the prime authority to examine the transatlantic air deal, to seek concessions from the two companies.
"We cannot say that this is the end. Whatever the parties say, they must move now," the source said.

Van Miert has threatened the British authorities with legal action if they fail to address the Commission's competition concerns. The Commission shares authority with Britain to vet the deal between BA and AMR's American, which will create the world's largest airline grouping.

Under article 89 of the treaty of Rome, it must work in cooperation with the British authorities when investigating the case but if needed "it shall propose appropriate measures" to ensure fair competition.
